subject: [PATCH v2] btrfs: properly cleanup replace_task when the replace failed to start

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that btrfs_dev_replace_cancel() leaves replace_task set every time due to the return of -ECANCELED from btrfs_scrub_dev(), and requested additional paths be covered in the changelog

Reviewer Qu Wenruo confirmed that the real work of dev-replace has finished, implying that the patch is correct and no further action is needed.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that resetting replace_task too early in btrfs_dev_replace_start() creates a window where the rwsem can be taken again, potentially leading to a deadlock, and suggested updating replace_state before clearing replace_task.
reviews.raw_body:
That "very hard to hit" was for the old code before the fix, but indeed 
Claude found an extra path that cancel can always leave that stale 
replace_task.

---

Yes.

The real work of dev-replace has all finished.

---

Alright, I guess the model you're using is digging deeper than opus.

It looks like we should not reset replace_task until the replace_state 
is also updated.

Or during the transaction commit, it will lead to the same problem.

We rely on btrfs_dev_replace_is_ongoing() to return false to release 
rwsem early and avoid the deadlock.

So the early reset leaves a window we can deadlock again.

Will send an update to this patch.

Thanks,
Qu

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Btrfs device replacement code where the replace_task was not being properly cleaned up when the replacement failed to start or was cancelled. The patch moves the assignment of dev_replace->replace_task below the replace_state switch, clears it when btrfs_start_transaction() fails, and clears it at the top of btrfs_dev_replace_finishing(). This ensures that the replace task is always properly released, even in cases where the replacement fails or is cancelled.
